experiment: Three-test comparison of temporal independence diagnostics
notes: Analysis only: reads all 600 saved Humanoid trajectories (20 arms, expected 30 observations per arm/iteration). No simulation or training.
Settings are fixed before this comparison; no search for settings giving a desired rejection rate, smoothing, monotonic enforcement, or selective trajectory removal.

AutoHSIC follows the U-centered portmanteau statistic and lag-independent wild bootstrap of Li, Xu and Zhou (2026), arXiv:2605.22025. Its bootstrap calibration is asymptotic, especially relevant for short prefixes.

BDS applies the m=2 correlation-integral statistic separately to each coordinate, using permutation rather than asymptotic normal calibration. The permutation-invariant standard-error factor cancels in the comparison. Twice the smaller coordinate p-value gives one Bonferroni-adjusted trajectory p-value.

BDS applied coordinate-wise can miss purely cross-coordinate lag dependence. All three diagnostics use an iid null for calibration; they do not isolate independence from changing marginal distributions.
Rejection proportions are pointwise across horizons, which share trajectories. Their direction and rate of change are outcomes, not configurable targets.
